sonnet.problem: Card 2 says the disciples' hands were 'defiled, that is, unwashed.' That points straight at the answer to card 3, 'Wash their hands ceremonially.'
sonnet.rule: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

sonnet.problem: Isaiah appears for the first time in this passage with no short label saying who he is, such as 'Isaiah, a prophet.' The label is given for Moses on card 12.
sonnet.rule: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

sonnet.problem: Card 15 (7:13, they nullify the word of God by their tradition) makes the same point as card 10 (7:8, they disregarded God's commandment to keep the tradition of men), so the same point is asked twice.
sonnet.rule: Two lines that make the same point get one question.

sonnet.problem: The card tells that food 'goes into the stomach and then is eliminated,' which is the body's private matters, and it carries a cookie joke.
sonnet.rule: A card that tells death, violence, abuse, serious sin or the body's private matters has no joke.

sonnet.problem: The card asks whether envy is on a list the baker hasn't been told yet. Card 10 stops at adultery, so the baker can't reason it out and can only guess. Envy is also not a standout item on the list.
sonnet.rule: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.
